Q: How to install a particular version of click? A:

You have two different errors -there ,and a version conflict you will have to resolve. gitsome needs an old click, and flask needs a new click. The only way out is to findout what package has gitsome as dependency and try to update that one - or just update gitsome, to a version that accepts a newer "click".

Q: scanf_s not enough arguments passed for format string(Visual Studio) A:

As the error message indicates, there is a missing argument in scanf_s("%s", st[i].name). According to the Annex K of the C Standard, you should pass the length of the destination array for a %s conversion. The char pointer should be followed by an extra argument of type rsize_t indicating the number of elements in the array pointed to by the previous argument:

K.3.5.3.2 The fscanf_s function

The fscanf_s function is equivalent to fscanf except that the c, s, and [ conversion specifiers apply to a pair of arguments (unless assignment suppression is indicated by a *). The first of these arguments is the same as for fscanf. That argument is immediately followed in the argument list by the second argument, which has type rsize_tand gives the number of elements in the array pointed to by the first argument of the pair.

K.3.5.3.4 The scanf_s function

The scanf_s function is equivalent to fscanf_s with the argument stdin interposed before the arguments to scanf_s.

The type rsize_t is identical to the type size_t but has a restricted range of 0 to RSIZE_MAX.

On the other hand, the Microsoft Documentation for this function differs on the type for the number of elements: it specifies in a highlighted note that reads:

The size parameter is of type unsigned, not size_t. Use a static cast to convert a size_t value to unsigned for 64-bit build configurations.

Therefore, if you want your program to compile with the Microsoft compiler, you should modify the code as:

        scanf_s("%s", st[i].name, (unsigned)sizeof(st[i].name));

But if you want the program to conform to the C Standard, the cast (unsigned) should be removed.

For this reason (among others), the functions from Annex K are not portable across architectures and are not even supported on many of them. Consider using standard, well defined functions such as scanf and pass the maximum number of bytes to read as:

        scanf("%9s", st[i].name);

You can disable the warning emitted by Microsoft Visual Studio about scanf by adding these lines before including <stdio.h>:

#ifdef _MSC_VER
#define _CRT_SECURE_NO_WARNINGS
#endif

Finally, note that you must check the return value of scanf, scanf_s and all related functions to detect invalid or missing input and avoid further undefined behavior. scanf will return 1 if a word was read into the name array and 0 or EOF otherwise.
